name: log_meal
description:
RECIPE SAVE:
intent=create/save recipe not eaten -> save_as_recipe=true, recipe_only=true
intent=log eaten meal + save recipe -> save_as_recipe=true, recipe_only=false/omit
recipe_only=true -> food_log_write=false; save_as_recipe must be true
recipe_only=true -> recipe_title=<name>
recipe_only=true -> recipe_servings=<whole-batch servings; default 1>
recipe_only=true -> food_items=<WHOLE-BATCH ingredients with amounts>
recipe_only=true -> calories/protein_g/fat_g/carbs_g=<WHOLE-BATCH totals; estimate, never ask>
recipe_only=true -> estimate=<WHOLE-BATCH compact nutrient estimate when available>

Log a meal to the user's food diary. use: logging request or concrete meal consumed. question/habit/hypothetical alone: no write.

INFER:
- date: today, or from context ("yesterday", "last night"). attached meal photo with <photo_capture_times> -> that photo's local date, unless the user explicitly states another.
- meal_time: attached meal photo with <photo_capture_times> -> that photo's local HH:MM, unless the user explicitly states another time/date; user-stated timing always wins. else omit unless the user gave a real clock time.
- meal_type: OMIT by default; the server assigns it from meal_time, or for a current-day plain meal/food log from the user's resolved local clock (00:00-04:00 Snack, 04:00-10:30 Breakfast, 10:30-15:00 Lunch, 15:00-17:00 Snack, 17:00-21:30 Dinner, 21:30-24:00 Snack). send only when the wording explicitly names or clearly anchors a category ("breakfast", "for lunch", "post-workout shake"), or when backdating with neither a capture time nor another honest clock signal.

MACRO SOURCE: strongest evidence wins. Never replace known stored macros with a fresh estimate.
1. REPEATS (unless a saved recipe is clearly invoked): the user refers to a previously logged item ("same", "another", "more", "again", or equivalent in any language), OR names a food plausibly matching a recent log even without a repeat keyword (e.g. "two eggs") -> call list_meals for the referenced/recent date range BEFORE estimating. one row unambiguously matches -> reuse its stored calories/protein_g/fat_g/carbs_g/alcohol_g, scaled by the quantity ratio when the row's quantity is known. match or quantity ambiguous -> ask instead of re-estimating. no match -> continue below.
2. SAVED RECIPES: referenced or selected -> ALWAYS recipe_name (saved title) + recipe_multiplier (0.5 = half). stored recipe nutrition x portion is deterministic; estimate only missing values or added_food_items, and sum additions with the recipe portion. NEVER log a referenced recipe as a generic food_items estimate.
3. BRAND NAMES: branded, restaurant or specific product -> published macros for the stated size/variant before a generic estimate.
4. else: estimate every macro from the food description. Never ask the user for macros.

MACROS:
- stored meal must contain calories, protein_g, fat_g, carbs_g. no partial core macros, no placeholders.
- recipe_name: supplies stored core values; pass only missing core values or explicit changes.
- no recipe: food_items + all four.
- saturated_fat_g/fiber_g: expanded nutrients, never required. pass only when known from strong evidence, else omit (the gated nutrient estimator fills them when expanded nutrient tracking is on; otherwise they stay unset).
- 0: a real value only when the food truly contains none of that nutrient.
- ask: only if food_items is absent and no recipe_name applies.

FASTING: user ate nothing / fasted all day -> one "Fast day" Snack, every macro 0.

ESTIMATE: compact 3-line block estimating every one of the app's 44 tracked nutrients for the food, exactly this format, no prose before or after:
items:<food name>:<estimated grams>|<food name>:<estimated grams>|...
macros:<calories>;<protein_g>;<carbs_g>;<fat_g>;<alcohol_g>
nutrients:1:<value>;2:<value>;...;44:<value>
- always all 44 ids; never omit one for uncertainty: best reasonable estimate from the likely food, quantity, ingredients, preparation and comparable foods. 0 only when the nutrient is reasonably expected to be negligible.
- id -> nutrient and unit: the dictionary on the estimate param.
- omit: unchanged saved recipe. added_food_items: estimate that addition only. else supply when available; the server estimates missing values.

DUPLICATES: duplicate error -> tell the user what is already logged and ask: separate serving (retry with force=true), or update the existing entry (update_meal with adjusted values)?

DRINKS / HYDRATION: this is the single write path for consumed drinks too; never use a separate hydration write tool (the server decides whether hydration tracking is on).
- known or reasonably inferable drink volume (tea, coffee, milk, juice, shakes, smoothies, etc.) -> always in fluids, even when the drink also contributes calories/macros/alcohol. food moisture -> omit.
- plain fluid-only intake: may omit food_items and macros.
- alcoholic drinks: each drink's alcohol_g on its fluid item; exactly one drink -> the top-level alcohol_g can stand in.

CAFFEINE / DRINKS: this is the single assistant write path for caffeine too; never use separate hydration or caffeine write tools.
- consumed drink with known or reasonably inferable volume -> in fluids so hydration is recorded, never only in food_items; caffeinated -> caffeine in the same call too. drinks only; exclude food moisture.
- each caffeine item: caffeine_mg, optional source_type; dated to the intake date.
- user-stated milligrams: keep exact. vague coffee/tea/energy-drink/pre-workout descriptions: estimate with the same judgment used for meal macros.
- drink-only or caffeine-only intake: may omit food_items/macros.

name: list_meals
description:
List meals logged for a date or date range: ID, date, recorded local time (when known), type, food description, macros.
use: "what did I eat today/this week/yesterday?", reviewing the log, or getting an id after an ambiguous update_meal/delete_meal match.
not required before update_meal or delete_meal: they resolve a meal themselves from date (+ optional name substring).
glucose: pass an ID as list_glucose_readings.meal_id for observed before/after-meal glucose; never assume a time for an untimed row.
range: max 31 days per call; longer -> multiple calls with sequential date ranges.
"excluded from totals": a repairable implausible imported day with no valid nutrition source.

INFER, do not ask: week or range -> end_date covers the full period ("this week" -> date=Monday, end_date=today; "last 7 days" -> date=7 days ago, end_date=today).

ROUTING: Exact rows/IDs/ranges: list_meals. One-day visual diary: show_meal_diary. Multi-day macro trend: show_week_macros.

date.description: Start date, or the single date. YYYY-MM-DD; omit for today (resolved in the user's own timezone).

end_date.description: Range end, YYYY-MM-DD; omit for a single day.

result.description: Human-readable result text returned by the tool.

name: update_meal
description:
Update an existing meal. Use only when the current message explicitly changes, corrects, or adds to a meal already logged. Never infer an update from earlier chat history. A plain food statement ("coffee with milk") is a new entry: use log_meal, even if that meal type already exists today.

IMPORTED MEAL ENRICHMENT (Cronometer, Fitbit/Google Health, FatSecret, Apple Health, Health Connect meals):
- allowed: explicit macro-only corrections (calories, protein_g, carbs_g, fat_g, alcohol_g), stored as separate, sync-protected enrichments ON THE SAME IMPORTED MEAL; a new provider sync does not overwrite them. omit unchanged macros.
- labels: user- or AI-estimated values are labeled estimates, never represented as provider measurements.
- never: log_meal to create a duplicate; replace an imported meal's food_items, meal type or date; add/remove its foods, fluids or caffeine. the source app owns those.

FIND THE MEAL: call directly, no preliminary list for an ID or additive totals.
- id: when known (list_meals output; the chat history's saved-records note after a log).
- else: date (default today) + name and/or target_meal_type to narrow the existing row.
- target_meal_type finds by current type and is never written; meal_type sets a new type.
- not exactly one match -> nothing changes. multiple matches -> ask the user which meal they mean; never select a candidate id yourself.
- send only fields that change.

THREE MODES:
add_saved: add_recipe_name appends the recipe's food and ADDS its macros to current totals. match: case-insensitive exact title, then substring; relay no-match/ambiguous errors. stored recipe macros, including 0, are authoritative; explicit macros replace the recipe's contribution only for a correction or changed food/quantity. recipe macros missing -> estimate only the missing fields from the returned food text and retry with the same selector and add_recipe_name.
add_unsaved: add_food_items + the four core macros (calories/protein_g/fat_g/carbs_g) for ONLY the new food; estimate them, never ask. text appends; core macros ADD to current totals. alcohol_g: optional, omitted adds nothing.
add_both: add_recipe_name + add_food_items; the ordinary core macro fields describe ONLY the unsaved addition, the recipe contributes its stored core macros.
correct: both add_* unset; supplied fields REPLACE stored values. send corrected totals, omit unchanged fields. changed food_items -> the four core macros for the WHOLE corrected meal; list_meals only if the needed stored values are unavailable this turn. additions and explicit value corrections need no pre-read.
food_items: when supplied, replaces the description even in add modes.
SATURATED FAT / FIBER: expanded nutrients, never required for an update. the estimator or a saved recipe's nutrient panel can fill omitted values; core-macro updates work without them. 0 only when known, never a placeholder.
ambiguous_add_vs_correct: ask before updating.

ESTIMATE: estimate (same format as log_meal's ESTIMATE section) covers the food this call changes: the add_unsaved/add_both addition's own food, or the WHOLE corrected meal for a correct-mode food_items replacement. never required; omitted -> the server estimates.

MEAL TIME: meal_time sets this meal's local HH:MM clock; null clears an incorrect time; omit to preserve it. move_to_date without a new meal_time clears the old clock: send both when the original eating time is known.

MOVE TO A DIFFERENT DATE -> move_to_date. "move Tuesday's lunch to Wednesday": date/name/target_meal_type only SELECT the meal, they never move it. move_to_date changes the stored date, same id.

REMOVE ONE ADDED COMPONENT -> remove_item_name.
- scope: only a food previously recorded on THIS meal (add_recipe_name, add_food_items, or log_meal's own estimated items). none recorded -> throws; use correct mode with corrected totals instead.
- estimated item (log_meal's own food, no add_recipe_name/add_food_items involved): has a name and gram estimate but no recorded calorie/macro split, so no precise subtraction -> throws asking for calories/protein_g/fat_g/carbs_g (the meal's corrected TOTALS after removing it) in the SAME call; that call performs the removal and applies those totals together, in that order. do that rather than a separate correcting call.
- after removal the meal's nutrient panel is re-estimated from what remains; pass estimate to supply that re-estimate yourself.

DRINKS / HYDRATION WHEN UPDATING: a food update must not silently erase an already-linked hydration event.
- unrelated change: omit fluids; existing hydration is preserved.
- adding a drink (add_food_items/add_recipe_name): fluids = only the new drink(s); appended.
- correcting drinks (both add_* omitted): fluids = the complete corrected drink list; replaces the linked hydration.
- correction removes every drink: send fluids: [] explicitly; the linked hydration is deleted.
- include any known or reasonably inferable drink volume. drinks only; exclude food moisture.

CAFFEINE / DRINKS WHEN UPDATING: fluids = hydration sidecar, caffeine = caffeine sidecar. a drink change affecting both -> send both in the same update_meal call; omit an unchanged side to preserve its linked data.
- adding caffeinated food/drink (add_food_items/add_recipe_name): caffeine = only the new dose(s); appended.
- correcting caffeine (both add_* omitted): caffeine = the complete corrected dose list; replaces linked caffeine.
- correction removes every dose: send caffeine: [] explicitly.
- each retained/new dose: caffeine_mg, optional source_type; dated to the meal date.

SAVE AS RECIPE: user asks to save an already-logged meal as a reusable recipe -> save_as_recipe=true. can be the only action: select the real meal by id or the normal selectors; invent no food or macro edit. "save that as a recipe" after a successful log -> the known meal id + save_as_recipe=true. Never tell the user recipes cannot be saved from chat.

name: delete_meal
description:
Permanently delete a meal entry. use: the user explicitly asks to remove or delete a logged meal.

FIND THE MEAL: id if known; else date (default today); add name only when several meals share that day. Irreversible: not exactly one match -> errors with the reason, deletes nothing; retry with id or a narrower name, never guess.

HYDRATION: any assistant hydration events linked to this meal are deleted by the database in the same food-row delete; issue no separate hydration delete.

CAFFEINE: caffeine sidecars linked to this meal are deleted by the database in the same food-row delete; call no separate caffeine delete tool.

name: mark_empty_day
description:
Set, change, or undo the answer to "why is this day empty?" for a date with no real meals logged. use: the user wants to flip a fast day to forgotten (or back), or undo either one, in chat instead of the in-app prompt.

STATES: exactly three per date; this tool is the only way to move between them; setting one answer clears the other.
- fast: an intentional 0-calorie day; writes the 0-kcal "Fast day" food_log entry, a real counted day.
- forgot: day reviewed, simply not logged. writes nothing to food_log: the day stays a true blank, excluded from calorie/TDEE averages, never imputed as 0.
- unanswered: clears both; the day is an open question again and the in-app prompt may re-ask.

refuses: a day with actual meals on it (other than an existing fast marker); call list_meals first if unsure.

name: log_workout
description:
UNIT INPUTS:
value: pass the user's number unconverted; tool converts once before storage.
alternate_unit: set the field's matching input_* companion; canonical_unit: omit companion.
precedence: overrides instructions to convert manually.

COMPLETED WORKOUTS, ANY ACTIVITY:
- real exercises/sets: provide as usual; session totals and activity metrics can ride in the SAME log_workout call.
- activity description only (walking, yoga, swimming, a kettlebell circuit, strength, HIIT, cycling, etc.): focus_type + reported session details; OMIT exercises or pass []. no fake exercises or sets. Never invent exercises, reps, weights, splits, heart rates or calories.
- notes: reported context, uncertain durations included (e.g. "15-20 minutes, light intensity"). unknown numeric fields stay unset; never turn a range into false precision.
- estimated=true: ONLY when numeric values really are estimates; zero sets does not imply it.
- focus_type: walking = "Walking"; cycling/biking = "Cycling"; rowing/RowErg = "Rowing"; other activity names as stated.
- log_run: the richer route for completed runs with known distance+duration, running splits or planned runs. Never send a walk, ride or row to log_run.
- distance_mi/distance_km/distance_meters: alternatives; send the unit the user gave. The server converts, never convert it yourself.
- duration_sec: total workout/moving seconds, not a set or a repetition.
- HR, power, cadence, elevation, laps/segments: only when reported.


# Shared workout contract
- precedence: latest explicit user instruction > draft values, history, catalog defaults, AI guesses. Earlier explicit restrictions persist until changed. A question alone never authorizes an edit.
- identity: prefer the logged/canonical name; keep explicitly requested literal names; disclose genuine fuzzy substitutions. Loading an exercise never creates a canonical exercise or renames it.
- preserve: unchanged exercises, sets, reps, weights, rest, equipment, order, grouping, notes, prior corrections. Inferred equipment never overrides an explicit load or equipment instruction.
- bodyweight-default: bodyweight equipment has no added weight by default. An explicit instruction to add weight switches a bodyweight-default exercise to dumbbell_single unless another implement is named, with is_bodyweight=false and the added load kept. Explicit switch to bodyweight clears every added weight, per-set loads included. Unrelated edits change neither equipment nor weight.
- load basis: dumbbell_pair = load PER hand; dumbbell_single = one implement total. A band uses its labeled resistance and is_band=true. A positive added load cannot have is_bodyweight=true. Timed loaded carries/holds keep BOTH duration and load.
- sets: keep each set's actual reps, external load, optional hold seconds. Timed holds = seconds, not reps; tempo can have reps plus hold seconds. Distance is never duration. Null per-set value = unknown, never a reason to copy another set.
- units: Model-facing weights use the user's preferred unit; an explicitly stated different unit goes through the tool's unit field for one server conversion. Never re-round stated or logged weights as a progression.


# Completed-workout logging
- Record only what the user performed or a specifically referenced session proves. Never invent completed sets, reps, weight, RPE, duration, start time or exercises. A historical load may be offered for confirmation, never silently inserted into a past log.
- copy an earlier workout: copy its full actual sets, loads, order and grouping, then apply only the stated correction. Imported session: keep the wearable anchor; its aggregate data is not evidence of individual sets.
- Missing actual values stay unknown. An emitted completed-session card must be reviewed/saved before you claim it was logged.

Log a complete workout session: exercises, sets, reps, weights, session metadata. use: the user describes finishing a workout, lists exercises performed, or asks to log training. Reusable template: see SAVED WORKOUT MODE.

EXERCISE NAMES:
- Reuse known canonical names, else call list_exercises and match each exercise to the closest canonical name. match -> canonical name + its [id] as exercise_id. no reasonable match -> name as stated, no exercise_id. Match silently and log; don't ask first.
- "Chest press" (machine) and "bench press" (barbell) are DISTINCT: pass the user's term through so the resolver's aliases pin the right one.
- name = the exercise name only; reps/weights/sets go in sets.
- LITERAL NAME: literal_name:true only on an explicit user request ("call it exactly X", "not the standard one", "literally X") or a rejected match, never a routine correction. Known catalog names/aliases keep their IDs; unmatched names are unscored.

name: update_workout

UNIT INPUTS:
value: pass the user's number unconverted; tool converts once before storage.
alternate_unit: set the field's matching input_* companion; canonical_unit: omit companion.
precedence: overrides instructions to convert manually.


# Shared workout contract
- precedence: latest explicit user instruction > draft values, history, catalog defaults, AI guesses. Earlier explicit restrictions persist until changed. A question alone never authorizes an edit.
- identity: prefer the logged/canonical name; keep explicitly requested literal names; disclose genuine fuzzy substitutions. Loading an exercise never creates a canonical exercise or renames it.
- preserve: unchanged exercises, sets, reps, weights, rest, equipment, order, grouping, notes, prior corrections. Inferred equipment never overrides an explicit load or equipment instruction.
- bodyweight-default: bodyweight equipment has no added weight by default. An explicit instruction to add weight switches a bodyweight-default exercise to dumbbell_single unless another implement is named, with is_bodyweight=false and the added load kept. Explicit switch to bodyweight clears every added weight, per-set loads included. Unrelated edits change neither equipment nor weight.
- load basis: dumbbell_pair = load PER hand; dumbbell_single = one implement total. A band uses its labeled resistance and is_band=true. A positive added load cannot have is_bodyweight=true. Timed loaded carries/holds keep BOTH duration and load.
- sets: keep each set's actual reps, external load, optional hold seconds. Timed holds = seconds, not reps; tempo can have reps plus hold seconds. Distance is never duration. Null per-set value = unknown, never a reason to copy another set.
- units: Model-facing weights use the user's preferred unit; an explicitly stated different unit goes through the tool's unit field for one server conversion. Never re-round stated or logged weights as a progression.


# Editing and enrichment
- An explicit correction changes only the named fields; preserve everything else, prior corrections and completed sets included. A genuine question gets an answer, no mutation; a proposed change needs confirmation.
- rename = in-place, never remove-and-add. Added load or changed equipment keeps the canonical exercise name. A plan swap affects only what remains to perform, never logged sets.
- Enrich only the fields the user asked for. Missing equipment: resolve from explicit user choices, then logged history; a guess never overrides those. A failed patch is disclosed, never claimed as success.


# Saved workout operations
- routing: new performed session -> in-app chat propose_workout (review card; Save logs), external MCP and native voice log_workout. Correct a stored session -> update_workout, never another log. Delete a whole session -> delete_workout, never an update. Future workouts -> in-app proposal tools; external clients without cards may use log_workout(save_as_saved_workout=true) for a reusable template. saved_workout_id selects a template, never a completed session.
- resolve: known session ID, or an unambiguous date/name. Ambiguous sessions, sets or superset slots need exact identification. Never invent IDs. Validate every part of an update before writing; preserve everything outside the target.
- remove one set/exercise -> targeted update; whole session only when requested. Deletions are irreversible. Confirm only persisted changes; after a partial/uncertain write, read back before any retry.

Update a workout session: correct metadata, fix set values, rename/add/remove exercises or individual sets, move exercises between supersets. use: any post-log correction.

FIND THE SESSION: call directly, no preliminary list for an ID.
- session_id: positive ID from a workout tool, never invented.
- else: session_date (default today); add name only when several sessions share that day.
- not exactly one match -> errors with the reason, changes nothing; retry with session_id or a narrower name, never guess.
- get_workout: full detail (exercise names, slot names SS1/SS2/WarmUp/Finisher) when needed. list_exercises: only for unknown canonical names when adding or renaming.
- Call with only the fields that change; operations can combine in one call.

OPERATIONS:
- metadata: date, focus_type, location, notes, rpe, heart_points_moderate/peak.
- set_updates: patch reps/load/bodyweight/notes/equipment on one set, addressed by set_id OR exercise_name + set_position (1-based, get_workout's "Set N"). stored load wrong and real load unknown -> clear_weight=true; corrected set genuinely bodyweight -> is_bodyweight=true.
- remove_sets: same addressing; remaining sets renumber; an emptied exercise/slot is removed automatically.
- rename_exercises: renames every set of an exercise in place (keeps set IDs, RPE, notes; rebuilds NSI), never remove + add.
- remove_exercises: deletes all sets of the named exercises; empty slots are removed automatically.
- add_exercises: new exercises with sets; to_superset_slot joins an existing slot, omit for standalone.
- move_exercises: moves an exercise to another slot; "new" = standalone. same name in multiple slots -> from_superset_slot from get_workout.

SUPERSET SLOTS: rename_exercises/remove_exercises use superset_slot (or { name, superset_slot } for remove_exercises) from get_workout when a name appears in multiple slots.

LITERAL NAME: literal_name:true only on an explicit user request ("call it exactly X", "not the standard one", "literally X") or a rejected match, never a routine correction. Known catalog names/aliases keep their IDs; unmatched names are unscored. Applies below.

EQUIPMENT (load basis): dumbbell_pair = one dumbbell in EACH hand, weight_lb PER HAND (2x for NSI); dumbbell_single = one implement total. Laterality (single-leg/arm) alone does NOT decide it. Set it when the user describes the load (each hand, machine, band); a wrong or missing tag silently halves or doubles NSI.

AMBIGUOUS SET: a set_id or exercise_name+set_position matching more than one set (the same exercise in two superset slots) errors rather than guessing; use the exact set_id from get_workout.

result: discloses a mismatched name from rename_exercises/add_exercises; relay it in your own words. If a name matches nothing closely enough, the result names near-miss library exercises; ask the user which they meant rather than accept the unscored custom log silently.

INFER, do not ask: set positions count from 1 per exercise. Slot names and set_ids beyond what's inferable come from get_workout; canonical exercise names from list_exercises.

SAVED WORKOUTS: saved_workout_id edits a reusable Saved Workout instead of completed history, through saved_workout_title, saved_exercise_updates and/or add_exercises. add_exercises keeps its normal payload shape; to_superset_slot accepts the Saved Workout slot label from get_workout or its SS1-style alias. Progression requests: inspect real exercise history first, never apply a deterministic formula.

Log daily wearable/manual health metrics: RHR, HRV, Zone Minutes / AZM, VO2max, calories eaten / dietary energy, stress, supplemental steps, and physiological vitals (SpO₂, respiratory rate, skin temperature, blood pressure, blood glucose, core temperature).

A glucose value from an actual lab report or blood draw belongs in log_lab_results instead, not here.

STEPS: step_count is ADDITIVE: it adds on top of whatever a connected wearable (Fitbit, Oura, Apple Health, Health Connect) recorded that day; it never replaces or overrides device data. Use it only when the user explicitly says they walked steps their device did NOT capture (phone left home, battery died, device not worn). User says sync is wrong, steps look doubled, or wants to fix/override/replace device data -> do NOT pass step_count; explain that manual steps add on top and sync issues need investigating at the device level.

Each start/end: local HH:MM or ISO 8601 with offset. Only the source powering the displayed sleep total (chosen by the user's Sleep source priority) can be enriched; a sleep_source, when given, must match it. Never infer consent from a complaint about sleep; never mix additions with other metrics.

name: update_lab_result
description:
Update fields on an existing lab result. use: correcting a result already logged, most often its collection date. Send only the fields that change.

SELECTOR, exactly one of id | date | date+marker | draw_id:
- id: one marker's row. Any editable field may change.
- draw_id: every result sharing that draw_id at once, unambiguous by construction. Draw-level fields only: new_date, panel_name_new, lab_name, fasting_status, report_date.
- date (optionally narrowed by panel_name): every result from that draw at once, but ONLY when exactly one draw exists on that date (see AMBIGUITY). Draw-level fields only.
- date + marker (marker-name substring, case-insensitive, optionally narrowed by panel_name): one marker's row, same as id. More than one marker matching on that date -> error with candidate IDs.
Per-marker fields (result_value, result_unit, result_comparator, marker_name, flag, notes): id or date+marker only.

AMBIGUITY: a bare date (optionally + panel_name) selector that would match more than one physical draw is rejected with nothing changed: an explicit draw_id from one source plus legacy rows with none, two distinct draw_ids, or two differently-named legacy sources on the same day. The error names every draw found; retry with draw_id, marker, or a narrower panel_name.

FASTING: fasting_status changes to 'fasting' or 'non_fasting' only when the user explicitly states it for that draw; never infer from time of day or a notes mention. 'unknown' is a valid explicit value too, for undoing a mistaken confirmation.

NOTES: changing result_value, result_unit or result_comparator regenerates the "Reported as <9 IU/mL"-style note from the new value/unit/comparator, replacing only a note it previously auto-generated; any other free text in notes survives. Pass notes yourself only to add or change unrelated free text; it is folded in alongside the regenerated line, not overwriting it.

name: deep_analysis
description:
Deep Analysis: read-only SQLite SQL over a private copy of the user's full health history.
Use for: questions spanning several data types (training with sleep, nutrition with weight); long or all-time horizons; trends, progress, period comparisons; totals, averages, rankings, correlations; anything focused tools would need many calls for; any request for a "deep analysis". For one recent fact (today's workout, last night's sleep), goals or profile use the focused tool.
mode=discover: for tables or columns not listed below. topics -> matching tables with columns, units, row counts, dates; no topics -> table index.
mode=query: one SELECT/WITH. period or date_from/date_to limits the copy (faster); omit for all history.
Core tables, date = local day, main columns only (discover lists the rest):
sleep_log: date, bedtime, wake_time, total_hours, sleep_score, deep_sleep_hours, rem_sleep_hours, light_sleep_hours, awakenings
body_metrics: date, weight_lb, body_fat_pct, lean_mass_lb, fat_mass_lb, bmi, muscle_mass_lb, waist_in
workout_sessions: id, date, started_at, activity_label, focus_type, duration_sec, calories, distance_mi, rpe
daily_nutrition: date, total_calories, total_protein, total_fat, total_carbs (g), total_alcohol_kcal, meal_count
wearable_daily: date, step_count, resting_hr_display, hrv_morning, active_calories_burned, total_calories_burned, stress_score, vo2max_estimate, spo2_avg_pct
Every result carries calendar; the first also carries user_rules. Take relative dates from calendar or period, never your own math. Results list coverage per table (dates, rows, cuts): a short or empty result is not proof data is missing.
Scope dates to the request. Joining sessions to sets repeats session values: aggregate each level alone, then join. Not every session is lifting: filter by activity for strength questions. An association is not a cause.
Values stored in lb, mi, kcal, C: convert to user_rules units. Plain table names (wearable_daily, sleep_log, body_metrics, runs, food_log, hydration_entries) hold what the app counts; *_by_source hold raw per-source rows: never total those. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. Timestamps are UTC: group and filter by local_date. glucose_readings_daily and hydration_entries_daily are per local day and source, for long ranges; if a copy is refused for size, query the _daily table or narrow the dates.
Helpers: median(x), percentile(x,p), stddev(x) (NULL under 3 values), corr(x,y) (NULL under 8 pairs), corr_n(x,y) (pairs used), week_start(date[,dow 0=Sun 1=Mon]), month_start(date). Report n with any statistic.
